resources.string: When enabled, reconnects an already enabled Nexus service while the app is running. No LSPosed required; other services are preserved.
Recovery is enabled. It checks the actual connection and stops after three failed attempts. Turning off system accessibility is respected.
Requires existing Root authorization. Standard accessibility remains available without Root.
Enable Nexus in system accessibility settings first. Recovery will not turn on a service you disabled.
Reconnecting Nexus and waiting for the actual service connection. You can turn recovery off to stop further attempts.
Waiting before the next attempt to avoid repeatedly restarting the service.
Automatic recovery stopped after three attempts. Check system accessibility settings, then retry if needed.
A previous repair was interrupted. Check and re-enable Nexus in system accessibility settings before continuing; automatic writes are paused.
Unable to save the recovery setting. Try again.
The service has not reconnected. Recovery may retry within its limit; check system settings if it continues to fail.
Resets the attempt limit. It does not grant Root or enable a disabled system service.
Nexus is the last enabled accessibility service. To avoid Android turning off accessibility during a rebind, re-enable Nexus in system settings.
